request.input: From your answer, I'll assume I should buy a dedicated alarm clock and keep my phone out of my bedroom. Right?

content.text: We need to respond to user's confirmation. They are asking: "From your answer, I'll assume I should buy a dedicated alarm clock and keep my phone out of my bedroom. Right?" So we should confirm, but also add nuance: yes, that's the core, but also mention that if they can't buy one immediately, they can use alternatives. Also emphasize that the key is to remove the phone from the bedroom to break the cycle. Keep it concise and supportive.

Yes, exactly. That’s the core move: **get a dedicated alarm clock, and keep your phone out of your bedroom entirely.** 

That one change does most of the heavy lifting — it removes the temptation at the exact moment you’re most vulnerable (lying in bed, tired, bored). You won’t have to rely on willpower because the phone simply won’t be there.

If you can’t buy an alarm clock right away, you can use an old phone (airplane mode) or a smart speaker as a temporary alarm. But the goal is the same: **your main phone sleeps in another room, not next to you.**

Once that’s in place, the other tips (like the brain dump and getting out of bed if you can’t sleep) become much easier to follow. You’ve got this.
